cc.t: I'm twenty-nine years old.
Eight months ago, I received a kidney.
Now there is an infection, and that kidney is failing.
I'm telling you this because nobody explained how this system works, until it was too late for me to use it.
I was handed pamphlets. Consent forms. A list of phone numbers.
Nobody told me I had rights.
Nobody taught me what to ask.
Nobody told me what the system does with a patient who stays quiet.
Then I found the Cold Ischemia Foundation.
It was built by a patient who has had three kidney transplants, and by Marie, his wife, the care partner who stood beside him through all three.
Its tools, guides and research are free.
A two-week course on the history and the money behind your own treatment.
A guide for the first twenty-four hours after a dialysis discharge notice, down to the word-for-word script.
A situation room that tells you who to call, in what order, and writes the letter.
A handbook for talking to your care team, with the chapter I wish I had read first: the authority you already have.
And a one-hundred-nine-page field guide for anyone thinking about giving a kidney.
Here is what makes it different.
The Foundation says it takes no donations, and no funding or sponsorships from drug companies, device makers, dialysis companies, insurers, or hospital systems.
Its fees are only for services you request, at posted rates.
Don't take its word for it.
Ask any organization five questions. Who pays you? Who governs you? Who shapes your message? What can't you say? And who do you answer to?
Then ask this foundation the same five.
The Foundation is looking for leaders.
Patients who have been quiet for too long. Care partners who are tired of being invisible.
People who want to learn to speak up, and to help the next patient do the same.
It starts with free training. Ten modules. And a real person reads your application.
I may not get my kidney back.
But I can tell you what I wish someone had told me.
Learn your rights before you need them.
Ask who pays.
And find the people who will stand beside you.
